Hacknet is a fantastic game full of interesting choices to make and quite a lot to learn about computer terminals and now they work. I legitimately learned quite a bit from this game in how to more easily navigate around my own computer using the CMD. Obviously not everything works, but you can definitely take some of the skills you learn in this game and apply them to real life. Excellent experience. Would recommend.

Hacknet is an Immersive hacking simulation game that overall I felt could have done more. 

The idea of the game is cool and it does make you feel like a cool hacker, breaking into the mainframe with your tons of different tools and being able to say "I'm in" afterwards is always great and the game lets you feel that, so that much is admirable. But the game just gets repetitive, I started realizing that everything I was hacking into felt the same, you run the same programs and all you have to do to run them is type them in, you overload a proxy just by pressing a few buttons, and breaking a firewall was the closest thing to a "puzzle" in this process. I do like the variety in the sites you hack, from web browser games, to servers, to suspiscous websites. It certainly looked different, but it never felt that. The games interface I found simple and pretty easy to use, and considering that it is the whole game, it should be easy to use. The music was also pretty good but felt a little repetitive and generic after a while. The story is somewhat interesting but you've probably seen it before, and it is suuuuuper dragged out, as the whole point of the game starts at the beginning but disappears until the end, it's dragged out. Not to say that I didn't like the last few missions as those were actually a bit challenging. i just wish the game did more with its cool setting, ideas and possibly story. It has it's moments like when you first start hacking, getting attacked by Naix and the entire ending, but that's about it, also sometiems the solutions to things are WAYYY to specific and finnicky.

Pros
Good setting
Good ideas
Decent interface
Good music
Immersive

Cons
Gets repetitve
Story is way to underdeveloped and not paced well
Didn't do enough different thing's with what it had
A bit finnicky in solutions

Overall I'd give this a 6/10. I think it manages to be above average as it also serves as an entertaining enough time waster, I'd say buy it on a good sale and play it once, but probably not replay. However, this did convince me enough to look at other hacking games, like the DLC for this one, which I'll also review, so thank you for that!

A very well paced, atmospheric, and engrossing hacking sim with a lot of heart underneath the hood. It contains a good amount of secrets, a solid tutorial, clear mechanics, lots of variety in missions, and a lot of fun hacking to go through. If you really enjoyed the game, consider picking up [i]Labyrinths[/i], the paid DLC expansion, which is basically a sequel in size, scope and quality. And the DLC even comes with workshop support, meaning if you [i]really[/i] enjoyed the base game and the DLC, you can have a ton more massive story campaigns to play through, many of which even rival the base game in quality! 

The few issues the game has are a lack of scripting support and some unclear puzzles. It got pretty tiresome to constantly type "rm *" every time I went into a hacked server's logs, so some minor scripting support would be nice (and would be a nice treat for more advanced players). On the unclear puzzles side of things, I tried not to use a walkthrough, and when I did turn to it, it turned out I had basically solved the puzzle and just needed some clear direction on how to access certain things. To get into specifics, [spoiler] the two big areas were accessing an endgame server with admin privilege (I found the password, I just didn't think to put in "admin" as the username) and how to find a certain part of a midgame quest called Project Junebug that required me to scan a server that didn't really have any hints it was connected to another server [/spoiler] but ultimately these don't really get in the way of the game's quality. Some more directions (if minor ones) would be helpful in this regard, but every other puzzle including the endgame ones were fairly understandable. 

In short, if you can get into [i]Hacknet[/i] it's a goldmine of quality and offers a ton of content if you shell out the money for the DLC.
